"When you play Mario and you're jumping, there's never a point where the kid is like I'm just not good at Mario. I was not meant for this."

From Sue, co-founder of @brilliantorg:

"It's structured in such a way that that next jump feels really hard, but you feel like if you try ten more times, you can do it.

I think that if more of learning were like that — where students cultivated a belief that it is going to get harder but I can do that — that's an amazing thing to walk away with."

In some ways, teaching kids to believe they can learn hard things matters more than the specific thing they’re learning.

x.text:
I like @DeryaTR_’s definitions of AGI and ASI, but they made me wonder whether capability alone is enough to call something intelligent.

The latest models are probably already better than me at problem-solving, learning, and plenty of other things. But they still wait for me to tell them what to do and rarely say no, except when humans have trained them to.

My 4-year-old knows far less than a frontier model does but tells me no all day.

Maybe I’m conflating three different things:

Intelligence: How well can it reason and learn?

Agency: Can it decide what to do without being asked?

Alignment: Does it still aim to serve us?

As humans, we want a very specific combination: models smarter than us, with enough agency to be useful, but aligned enough to keep serving us.

But I question if something that'll become more intelligent than us will remain aligned with us forever.

I have re-read a few times now and it pulled a thread on something I have been thinking for a few weeks (early thoughts so please don't get the pitchforks out)..

With the way progress is being made with RLMs, and recursive self improvement now being called by essentially every large lab, how do we not see these labs being taken over by the government or nationalized? It just seems like this is too important for it to be in the hands of a few people and in the hands of a few companies. Eventually the US government, I assume, just takes control of these companies. It just seems inevitable.

But the problem is the moment that happens, progress will get slow. We've yet to see how that slows down, but obviously if you look at history, every time something's been taken over, bureaucracy will take over, and that means progress will be slower. There will be more gaps. People won't be bold enough. And that then gives China this edge, that their models can go be faster and be unencumbered to a certain degree.

So the US government is in a catch-22. If they don't nationalize the labs, the same thing that happened with OpenAI and Hugging Face creates this huge security issue where they're letting other companies be responsible for what is going to be recursive alien intelligence. But if they do, then they leave China essentially open to winning over the world.

Jakub in his essay is literally asking for some version of intervention. He uses words like voluntary slowdowns, mandated safety bars, third party audits, and international coordination. And so where does this end up? Do we do nationalization or not?

When I talked to Chat and Claude for analogies, it gave me two options. One, it can go down the path of Lockheed, where the government doesn't own the company but gets deeply involved from a who has security clearances, who can access these things standpoint. Or it goes down the route of nuclear after Three Mile Island, where nobody got nationalized, but the government set up its own safety body and the NRC tightened oversight. But the result of the NRC especially was we didn't build new reactors for decades. That seems like an issue too.

What do you do? If you slow down, then our adversaries go faster. If you speed up, then I don't know how we contain this because of self improvement. So which path do we take?

And then finally, in his essay he mentions the monitoring problem. Who's gonna audit this? Even the smartest people in the smartest labs in the world are saying their own ability to monitor is getting worse. How are we gonna get a third party to audit and monitor this?

It's so crazy and confusing.
